journeys.feature: Install with the web installer (defaults, local model found)
journeys.note: The install line in a terminal, then the browser installer. The browser opens on its own on a desktop; on a server the link is opened by hand (counted). A computer missing Docker also asks for its password.

steps.what: paste the install line and press Enter

journeys.feature: Create the first admin (passkey)
journeys.note: From the setup link, which fills in the setup code.

journeys.feature: First-run setup wizard, every step with its defaults
journeys.note: It asks only what has no default: the model provider, filled in from the local model found (and a budget for a cloud one). The survey's Lens started before its stand-in installer, so the model isn't set yet; after the real web installer, which sets it, the wizard doesn't open. The namespace, storage, apps and telemetry keep their defaults.

steps.what: Save and continue (Connect a model provider)

journeys.feature: Ask the first question from the welcome tour
Import a pasted transcript
Open a recording from the Library
Search for a word and see where it was said
Jump to a recording with Ctrl+K
Ask the assistant in Chat
Write a note

steps.what: Enter to go to the first line

journeys.feature: Add a topic
Make a pipeline from the standard steps
journeys.note: Lens guesses the name from the steps; it can be renamed on the pipeline's page.

journeys.feature: Make a nightly routine (sync sources, the default action)
journeys.note: Lens guesses the name from when it runs and what it does; it can be renamed later.

journeys.feature: Add the example skill to the assistant
Make a webhook sensor
Change the model's timeout
Add a person as a viewer
Make an API token
journeys.note: Lens guesses the name from the scope; it can be renamed in the list.

journeys.feature: Switch to another namespace
Connect an AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor) over MCP
journeys.note: Copy MCP address in the account menu; in the assistant: add a connector and paste the address; the assistant opens Lens's consent page, where the person allows it.

steps.what: in the assistant: add a connector, paste Lens's MCP address, add it

journeys.feature: Upload a transcript file
Watch a folder on this machine for new files
journeys.note: Needs rclone, as the Lens image has (CI copies the image's version); the folders offered are the allowed ones set at startup.

journeys.feature: Find an entity and see where it was mentioned
journeys.note: Its name opens its own page, /wiki/<namespace>/Raspberry_Pi, with its notes and every line that says it.

journeys.feature: Find a speaker in the graph of what was imported
journeys.note: The first namespace keeps its graph to itself, so the graph opens empty until it is picked as the namespace.

journeys.feature: Make a podcast from a recording
Save the namespace report as a PDF
journeys.note: The browser's print dialog does the saving (one click there, counted).

journeys.feature: Make a workflow
journeys.note: Lens guesses the name from what it runs on; it can be renamed on the workflow's page.

journeys.feature: Make a prompt template
journeys.note: Lens guesses the name from the kind; it can be renamed on the template's page.

journeys.feature: Make a namespace
Name a speaker
Merge two entities into one, then undo it
journeys.note: The merge happens at once and the notice has Undo, so nothing asks to confirm; Undo puts both back.

steps.what: Merge into the one it keeps

journeys.feature: Merge an entity into another from the graph, then undo it
journeys.note: Find the node, Merge in its panel, type the other's name and Enter; the notice has Undo, so nothing asks to confirm.

journeys.feature: Regenerate an answer, then switch back to the first version
journeys.note: In the conversation chat-ask started: Regenerate writes another answer beside it (2 / 2), and the arrow before the count shows the first again.

journeys.feature: Copy an answer
journeys.note: Continues chat-regenerate, in its conversation. Copy copies it as Markdown, its citations as footnotes; the arrow beside it has Copy text and Export.

journeys.feature: Export a conversation as a PDF
journeys.note: Continues chat-copy. The download icon in the conversation's header, then PDF. Where the server can make the PDF (Chromium, anytopdf or LibreOffice) the browser saves it; where it can't, the browser's print dialog opens on the conversation and does the saving (one click there, counted).

journeys.feature: Pick the tools and a tool-call limit for a conversation
journeys.note: Continues chat-export-pdf. The Tools chip beside the scope: switching one group off keeps the others (Auto goes off), and the limit starts at 10 calls. Each change is saved to the conversation as it's made, and new conversations start with it.

journeys.feature: Switch to a cloud model with an API key
journeys.note: What a Raspberry Pi install does after the installer: a cloud provider picked from the presets fills in its address and model, then a pasted key.

steps.what: OpenAI (fills in the address and the model)
